name: Severe Congenital Myopathy with Fiber-Type Disproportion

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Fiber-Type Disproportion Myopathy

criteria.description: Congenital onset of generalized muscle weakness and hypotonia
Muscle biopsy showing type 1 fiber atrophy with disproportionate fiber size difference (>12%) without other structural abnormalities
Identification of pathogenic variants in known associated genes (e.g., ACTA1, TPM3, SEPN1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital muscle weakness plus muscle biopsy demonstrating fiber-type disproportion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; exclusion of other congenital myopathies is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Type 1 muscle fiber atrophy with fiber size disproportion on biopsy

occasional.notes: Rarely observed, usually mild if present

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate elevation or normal)
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective muscle involvement and fatty infiltration
genetic: Pathogenic variants in ACTA1, TPM3, SEPN1, or other related genes
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating type 1 fiber atrophy with fiber size disproportion (>12%) without cores or other structural abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of nemaline rods on muscle biopsy
Often associated with respiratory failure and facial weakness
Variable clinical severity with axial weakness

redFlags: Severe feeding difficulties with failure to thrive
references: North KN, Laing NG, Wallgren-Pettersson C. Nemaline myopathy: current concepts. The ENMC International Consortium. Neuromuscul Disord. 1997;7(4):311-7.
Ryan MM, Schnell C, Strickland CD, et al. Congenital myopathies: clinical features and diagnosis. Neuromuscul Disord. 2001;11(4): 287-300.
Jungbluth H, Sewry CA, Muntoni F. Core myopathies. Semin Pediatr Neurol. 2011;18(4):239-49.
